Stage 2: BLUP-based individual-difference correlations (FDR-corrected). v2: confirmatory/exploratory component split; lmerTest dispatch hardening; partial eta-squared with 95% CI; cascade Satterthwaite -> Kenward-Roger -> Wald."

``` {r setup, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. Global Configuration & Environment
# ==============================================================================
# Note: knitr defaults buffer chunk output until completion. For long-running
# chunks (large LMM fits), we set R.options(progress = TRUE) and use
# flush.console() inside helpers (see flush_progress() below). When running
# interactively in RStudio (not via Knit), output is unbuffered automatically.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  results = "markup"   # default; ensures plain text streams correctly
)
options(scipen = 999, digits = 4)
set.seed(2024)

# Sum-to-zero contrasts: required for valid Type III ANOVA in the presence of
# interactions, and for interpretable zero-correlation random-effect parameterizations.
# Reference: Schad, Vasishth, Hohenstein, & Kliegl (2020) on contrast coding.
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Global Settings & Analysis Targets (SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Set experiment version to match upstream preprocessing pipeline output.
experiment_version <- "E2"  # Options: "E1" or "E2"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 2 trait groups. Each group is FDR-corrected independently, separating
# theory-driven hypotheses from broader exploratory tests. This prevents the
# dilution of confirmatory power that occurs when theoretically central traits
# share a multiple-testing burden with secondary exploratory dimensions.
#
# WHAT STAGE 2 TESTS: For each component x random-effect-term combination, do
# the per-subject BLUPs (best linear unbiased predictors of random slopes)
# correlate with the trait? A significant correlation indicates that the trait
# moderates the experimental effect on that ERP component.
#
# Group naming convention drives output directory names; keep names file-system
# safe (no spaces or punctuation other than underscores).
#
# CURRENT GROUPING (default):
#   Primary_TheoryDriven : SVO + Negative Affectivity (UG-relevant trait dimensions)
#   Exploratory_PID5BF   : Five remaining maladaptive personality dimensions
#   Exploratory_Rating   : Three deception-belief check ratings
#
# ALTERNATIVE GROUPINGS - uncomment exactly one to switch focus:
#
# Alt A: Rating-primary (cover-story-trust as the central moderator)
#   Primary_Ratings        = c("Rating_1", "Rating_2", "Rating_3"),
#   Exploratory_SVO_NegAff = c("SVO_angle", "Negative_Affectivity"),
#   Exploratory_PID5BF     = c("Detachment", "Antagonism", "Disinhibition",
#                              "Anankastia", "Psychoticism")
#
# Alt B: Two-tier - Rating primary, all personality traits collapsed
#   Primary_Ratings    = c("Rating_1", "Rating_2", "Rating_3"),
#   Exploratory_Trait  = c("SVO_angle", "Negative_Affectivity",
#                          "Detachment", "Antagonism", "Disinhibition",
#                          "Anankastia", "Psychoticism")
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
stage2_trait_groups <- list(
  Primary_TheoryDriven = c("SVO_angle", "Negative_Affectivity"),
  Exploratory_PID5BF   = c("Detachment", "Antagonism", "Disinhibition",
                           "Anankastia", "Psychoticism"),
  Exploratory_Rating   = c("Rating_1", "Rating_2", "Rating_3")
)

# Flat union retained for covariate loading (load_covariates filters by this).
stage2_traits <- unlist(stage2_trait_groups, use.names = FALSE)

# Post-hoc gating thresholds (v2: layered).
# Effects with omnibus interaction p < confirmatory_alpha enter the main report.
# Effects with confirmatory_alpha <= p < marginal_threshold are written to
# Supplementary as "marginal" simple-effect contrasts; they are NEVER reported
# as confirmatory evidence. p >= marginal_threshold: no simple-effect extraction.
confirmatory_alpha  <- 0.05
marginal_threshold  <- 0.10

# Component definitions per experimental design.
# 
# CONFIRMATORY components are present in BOTH experiments (E1 ∩ E2) and
# constitute the cross-experiment conceptual replication evidence:
#   FRN, N400, LPP_offer.
# 
# EXPLORATORY components differ between experiments and are not directly
# comparable cross-experiment:
#   E1: EPN (offer-locked; face occurred prior, so EPN here reflects offer
#       processing, NOT face-evoked perception).
#   E2: N170, EPN (face-evoked / face+offer simultaneous; functionally
#       distinct from E1 EPN).
# 
# Status per component is propagated to REPRODUCIBILITY.txt and Methods
# paragraph. All components run the same Stage 1 LMM pipeline; the
# confirmatory/exploratory distinction is a reporting-layer label.
# 
# CPP (response-locked) was previously included; v2 removes it as out of
# scope for the offer-phase analysis.
if (experiment_version == "E1") {
  confirmatory_components <- c("FRN", "N400", "LPP_offer")
  exploratory_components  <- c("EPN")
} else if (experiment_version == "E2") {
  confirmatory_components <- c("FRN", "N400", "LPP_offer")
  exploratory_components  <- c("N170", "EPN")
} else {
  stop("Configuration Error: Unknown experiment_version.")
}
analyze_stim_components <- c(confirmatory_components, exploratory_components)

# Helper to return component status for downstream reporting.
component_status <- function(comp_name) {
  if (comp_name %in% confirmatory_components) "confirmatory"
  else if (comp_name %in% exploratory_components) {
    if (experiment_version == "E1") "exploratory_offer_locked"
    else "exploratory_E2_only"
  }
  else NA_character_
}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

if(!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(
  here, readr, readxl, dplyr, tidyr, stringr, tibble, purrr,  # Data wrangling
  lme4, lmerTest,                                              # Modeling
  pbkrtest,                                                    # Kenward-Roger backend for lmerTest
  car, parameters, performance,                                # Diagnostics
  buildmer,                                                    # LRT-based structure search
  R.utils,                                                     # withTimeout for buildmer protection
  emmeans, effectsize,                                         # Marginal means, effect sizes
  sjPlot, sjmisc,                                              # tab_model, plot_model
  ggplot2, ggpubr, gridExtra,                                  # Publication visualization
  knitr, kableExtra,                                           # Markdown table rendering
  openxlsx                                                     # Legacy Excel export
)

# Inferential strategy: cascading method preference for LMM
# (Satterthwaite -> Kenward-Roger -> Wald). EEG analyses are pure LMM
# (Gaussian on amplitude in microvolts), so there is no GLMM branch.
# 
# Cascade rationale:
# (1) Satterthwaite F (lmerTest::anova): finite-DenDF F-test, preferred for
#     Type I error control at moderate N_subj (Luke 2017).
# (2) Kenward-Roger F (pbkrtest backend via lmerTest): conservative second-
#     order correction. Different numerical implementation than Satterthwaite,
#     can succeed when Satterthwaite hits Hessian inversion failure modes on
#     ZCP-form (e.g., (0 + factor | id)) random structures at large N.
# (3) Wald chi-square (car::Anova): final fallback. Anti-conservative for
#     finite N (Luke 2017 simulations show Type I error 6-8% at N_subj < 30
#     for omnibus tests). Logged in REPRODUCIBILITY.txt when invoked.
# 
# CRITICAL ENGINEERING DETAIL: lmerTest's Satterthwaite/KR dispatch requires
# the model object class to include "lmerModLmerTest". When fit via
# lme4::lmer() (rather than lmerTest::lmer()), the result is bare "lmerMod"
# and anova() falls through to lme4's base method which silently ignores
# the ddf argument and returns no Pr column. fit_stage1_bates therefore
# upgrades the final model class via lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest() before
# returning, and the ANOVA cascade independently re-checks. See bates-engine
# chunk for details.
# 
# Post-hoc contrasts via emmeans use asymptotic (z-test) df for computational
# stability on large datasets. At present DenDF magnitudes (DenDF >> 30),
# z-tests differ from Satterthwaite-based t-tests by less than 1% (Luke 2017).
emmeans::emm_options(lmerTest.limit = 1e7, pbkrtest.limit = 1e7,
                     lmer.df = "asymptotic")
options(lmerTest.limit = 1e7)
options(pbkrtest.limit = 1e7)

# Output directory tree organized by analytic stage and reporting target.
out_root    <- here("results", "EEG", paste0(experiment_version, "_TwoStage_Bates_Alday"))
out_stage1  <- file.path(out_root, "Stage1_TrialLevel")
out_stage2  <- file.path(out_root, "Stage2_BLUP_Correlations")
out_tables  <- file.path(out_root, "Tables_Manuscript")
out_suppl   <- file.path(out_root, "Supplementary")
for (d in c(out_stage1, out_stage2, out_tables, out_suppl)) {
  if (!dir.exists(d)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE)
}

cat(sprintf("Pipeline initialized for Experiment: %s\nRoot: %s\nStage 2 trait groups (%d total traits):\n",
            experiment_version, out_root, length(stage2_traits)))
for (gname in names(stage2_trait_groups)) {
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %s\n", gname,
              paste(stage2_trait_groups[[gname]], collapse = ", ")))
}

# Visual theme.
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
          theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top"))

colors_emo <- c('neu'="#8491B4",'aff'="#91D1C2",'dis'="#E64B35",'dom'="#F39B7F",'enj'="#3C5488")
labels_emo <- c('neu'='Neutral','aff'='Affiliative','dis'='Disgust','dom'='Dominance','enj'='Reward')
colors_off <- c('fair'="#2E86AB",'unfair'="#A23B72")
labels_off <- c('fair'='Fair', 'unfair'='Unfair')

custom_control <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 200000), calc.derivs = FALSE)

# Null-coalescing helper for safe attribute fallback.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Buildmer engineering helpers (defensive against deadlock on large datasets).
# 
# When N > 20K trials, lmerTest can cause buildmer's iterative LRT loop to hang
# (CPU 0%) because every internal anova() call triggers Satterthwaite Hessian
# inversion. We detach lmerTest before buildmer and reattach after. We also
# wrap buildmer in withTimeout to prevent unbounded waits.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
detach_lmerTest_safely <- function() {
  if ("package:lmerTest" %in% search()) {
    detach("package:lmerTest", unload = FALSE, character.only = FALSE)
    return(TRUE)
  }
  FALSE
}

reattach_lmerTest_safely <- function(was_detached) {
  if (isTRUE(was_detached)) suppressMessages(library(lmerTest))
  invisible(NULL)
}

run_buildmer_protected <- function(buildmer_fn, ..., timeout_sec = 1800) {
  was_lmerTest <- detach_lmerTest_safely()
  on.exit(reattach_lmerTest_safely(was_lmerTest), add = TRUE)
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    R.utils::withTimeout({
      buildmer_fn(...)
    }, timeout = timeout_sec, onTimeout = "error")
  }, TimeoutException = function(ex) {
    progress_log(sprintf("[TIMEOUT] buildmer exceeded %d seconds; aborting.",
                         timeout_sec), indent = 2)
    NULL
  }, error = function(e) {
    if (grepl("reached.*time.*limit|timeout", conditionMessage(e), ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[TIMEOUT] buildmer exceeded %d seconds; aborting.",
                           timeout_sec), indent = 2)
      NULL
    } else {
      progress_log(sprintf("[WARN] buildmer error: %s", conditionMessage(e)),
                   indent = 2)
      NULL
    }
  })
  
  result
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Progress reporting helpers.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# R Markdown can buffer cat() output until a chunk finishes, hiding progress
# during long-running operations. flush_progress() forces immediate display.
# Wall-clock timing is captured per stage to give the user realistic runtime
# expectations on subsequent components.
flush_progress <- function() {
  flush.console()
  if (interactive()) Sys.sleep(0)  # nominal yield
}

progress_log <- function(msg, indent = 0) {
  prefix <- strrep("  ", indent)
  cat(sprintf("%s%s\n", prefix, msg))
  flush_progress()
}

# Format an elapsed-time delta for log lines. Used to report duration of
# expensive operations (model fits, ANOVA, buildmer search).
format_elapsed <- function(t_start) {
  secs <- as.numeric(Sys.time() - t_start, units = "secs")
  if (secs < 60) sprintf("%.1fs", secs)
  else if (secs < 3600) sprintf("%dm%02ds", floor(secs / 60), round(secs %% 60))
  else sprintf("%dh%02dm", floor(secs / 3600), floor((secs %% 3600) / 60))
}

# Wrap an expression with start/end progress logs and elapsed time.
with_progress <- function(label, expr, indent = 1) {
  progress_log(sprintf("[%s] starting...", label), indent = indent)
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  result <- force(expr)
  progress_log(sprintf("[%s] done (%s).", label, format_elapsed(t0)),
               indent = indent)
  result
}
```

``` {r apa-module}
# ==============================================================================
# 2. Helper Functions (preserved from original script).
# ==============================================================================

# Universal type conversion, missing-value handling, and column purging.
kill_scipen <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), function(vec) {
      if (is.numeric(vec)) {
        vec <- format(round(vec, 4), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
      }
      vec <- ifelse(is.infinite(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(vec))), "Inf", vec)
      vec <- ifelse(is.na(vec) | vec == "NA", "-", as.character(vec))
      vec
    })) %>%
    dplyr::select(where(~ !all(. == "-")))
}

# APA significance star generator.
add_sig_stars <- function(p) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p)  ~ "-",
    p < 0.001 ~ "***",
    p < 0.01  ~ "**",
    p < 0.05  ~ "*",
    p < 0.1   ~ ".",
    TRUE      ~ "ns"
  )
}

# Map sum-coding suffixes back to interpretable factor-level labels.
beautify_labels <- function(df) {
  dict <- c(
    "\\bemotion1\\b"    = "emotion[neu-grand]",
    "\\bemotion2\\b"    = "emotion[aff-grand]",
    "\\bemotion3\\b"    = "emotion[dis-grand]",
    "\\bemotion4\\b"    = "emotion[dom-grand]",
    "\\boffer_type1\\b" = "offer_type[fair-grand]"
  )
  df %>% dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.character),
                              ~ stringr::str_replace_all(., dict)))
}

# Format ANOVA table to APA strings.
# v2: appends partial eta-squared with 95% CI for LMM (Gaussian) models.
# Effect-size computation uses effectsize::eta_squared() which handles
# both lme4 and lmerTest model classes. EEG analyses are pure LMM, so
# eta-squared is always meaningful here (no GLMM branch).
format_anova_apa <- function(anova_obj, model = NULL) {
  df_res <- as.data.frame(anova_obj) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Effect")
  
  get_col <- function(col_name) {
    if (col_name %in% names(df_res)) df_res[[col_name]] else rep(NA, nrow(df_res))
  }
  
  df_res <- df_res %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      F_val  = get_col("F value"),
      NumDF  = get_col("NumDF"),
      DenDF  = get_col("DenDF"),
      Df_val = get_col("Df"),
      Chisq  = get_col("Chisq"),
      p_val  = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(get_col("Pr(>F)"))     ~ get_col("Pr(>F)"),
        !is.na(get_col("Pr(>Chisq)")) ~ get_col("Pr(>Chisq)"),
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      Sig = add_sig_stars(p_val),
      p_str = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(p_val)  ~ "-",
        p_val < .001  ~ "< .001",
        TRUE          ~ paste0("= ", format(round(p_val, 3), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))
      ),
      APA_Report = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(F_val) & !is.na(NumDF) & !is.na(DenDF) ~
          sprintf("F(%s, %.2f) = %.2f, p %s", NumDF, DenDF, F_val, p_str),
        !is.na(F_val) & !is.na(NumDF) ~
          sprintf("F(%s) = %.2f, p %s", NumDF, F_val, p_str),
        !is.na(Chisq) & !is.na(Df_val) ~
          sprintf("\u03C7\u00B2(%s) = %.2f, p %s", Df_val, Chisq, p_str),
        TRUE ~ "[stat unrecognized]"
      )
    )
  
  # Partial eta-squared with 95% CI. Only computed for F-statistic rows
  # (LMM Satterthwaite/KR). Wald chi-square fallback rows show "-".
  eta_str <- rep("-", nrow(df_res))
  if (!is.null(model) && inherits(model, "merMod")) {
    eta_tab <- tryCatch(
      effectsize::eta_squared(anova_obj, partial = TRUE, ci = 0.95,
                              alternative = "two.sided"),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (!is.null(eta_tab) && nrow(eta_tab) > 0) {
      eta_df <- as.data.frame(eta_tab)
      param_col <- intersect(c("Parameter", "Effect"), names(eta_df))[1]
      eta_col   <- intersect(c("Eta2_partial", "Eta2"), names(eta_df))[1]
      lo_col    <- "CI_low"
      hi_col    <- "CI_high"
      if (!is.na(param_col) && !is.na(eta_col) &&
          all(c(lo_col, hi_col) %in% names(eta_df))) {
        for (i in seq_len(nrow(df_res))) {
          eff_name <- df_res$Effect[i]
          match_idx <- which(eta_df[[param_col]] == eff_name)
          if (length(match_idx) == 1) {
            eta_str[i] <- sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]",
                                  eta_df[[eta_col]][match_idx],
                                  eta_df[[lo_col]][match_idx],
                                  eta_df[[hi_col]][match_idx])
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  df_res$eta2_partial_95CI <- eta_str
  
  df_res <- df_res %>%
    dplyr::select(Effect, APA_Report, eta2_partial_95CI, Sig, p_val)
  beautify_labels(df_res)
}

# Format post-hoc emmeans output to APA strings.
# v2: appends 95% CI columns. EEG analyses operate on raw amplitude scale
# (microvolts, Gaussian), so no scale transformation (no OR, no percent
# change) is needed -- contrasts are reported directly in microvolts.
# Switches to z-statistic notation when df is infinite (asymptotic case).
format_posthoc_apa <- function(emm_df) {
  df_clean <- as.data.frame(emm_df)
  
  est_col <- intersect(names(df_clean),
                       c("estimate", "emmean", "response"))
  if (length(est_col) == 0) {
    trend_col <- grep("\\.trend$", names(df_clean), value = TRUE)
    est_col <- if (length(trend_col) > 0) trend_col[1] else names(df_clean)[2]
  } else {
    est_col <- est_col[1]
  }
  
  # CI columns. emmeans summary(infer=c(TRUE,TRUE)) emits CL columns, but
  # column naming varies:
  #   - "lower.CL" / "upper.CL"      (most cases)
  #   - "asymp.LCL" / "asymp.UCL"    (when df is Inf, e.g. asymptotic mode)
  # If neither is present (rare; happens when summary infer didn't fire),
  # synthesize from estimate +/- 1.96*SE (Wald-based asymptotic CI). This
  # ensures lower.CL / upper.CL columns ALWAYS exist, which matters because
  # dplyr::case_when() evaluates ALL RHS expressions regardless of LHS truth
  # value -- a missing column would error even on rows where the expression
  # is "not selected".
  if (all(c("lower.CL", "upper.CL") %in% names(df_clean))) {
    # already correctly named
  } else if (all(c("asymp.LCL", "asymp.UCL") %in% names(df_clean))) {
    df_clean$lower.CL <- df_clean$asymp.LCL
    df_clean$upper.CL <- df_clean$asymp.UCL
  } else if ("SE" %in% names(df_clean)) {
    # Synthesize Wald CI. Mark as fallback in case downstream wants to flag.
    df_clean$lower.CL <- df_clean[[est_col]] - 1.96 * df_clean$SE
    df_clean$upper.CL <- df_clean[[est_col]] + 1.96 * df_clean$SE
  } else {
    # No SE either: emit NA columns to keep the schema stable.
    df_clean$lower.CL <- NA_real_
    df_clean$upper.CL <- NA_real_
  }
  has_ci <- all(c("lower.CL", "upper.CL") %in% names(df_clean)) &&
            !all(is.na(df_clean$lower.CL))
  
  df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Sig = add_sig_stars(p.value),
      p_str = dplyr::case_when(
        p.value < .001 ~ "< .001",
        TRUE ~ paste0("= ", format(round(p.value, 3), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))
      )
    )
  
  # Stats_String: with CI when available, fall back to no-CI form otherwise.
  # Unit hint "muV" because EEG amplitudes are in microvolts.
  if ("t.ratio" %in% names(df_clean)) {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      Stats_String = dplyr::case_when(
        has_ci & is.infinite(df) ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f], z = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, lower.CL, upper.CL, t.ratio, p_str),
        has_ci ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f], t(%.2f) = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, lower.CL, upper.CL, df, t.ratio, p_str),
        is.infinite(df) ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), z = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, t.ratio, p_str),
        TRUE ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), t(%.2f) = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, df, t.ratio, p_str)
      )
    )
  } else if ("z.ratio" %in% names(df_clean)) {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      Stats_String = dplyr::case_when(
        has_ci ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f], z = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, lower.CL, upper.CL, z.ratio, p_str),
        TRUE ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), z = %.2f, p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, z.ratio, p_str)
      )
    )
  } else {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      Stats_String = dplyr::case_when(
        has_ci ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f], p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, lower.CL, upper.CL, p_str),
        TRUE ~ sprintf(
          "b = %.2f muV (SE = %.2f), p %s",
          .data[[est_col]], SE, p_str)
      )
    )
  }
  
  if (has_ci) {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>%
      dplyr::mutate(CI_str = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", lower.CL, upper.CL))
  }
  
  df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    dplyr::select(-p_str) %>%
    dplyr::relocate(Sig, .after = Stats_String)
  beautify_labels(df_clean)
}

# Extract fixed-effect coefficients with safe fallback.
format_coefs <- function(model) {
  tryCatch({
    coefs <- as.data.frame(parameters::parameters(model, effects = "fixed"))
    coefs %>% beautify_labels() %>% kill_scipen()
  }, error = function(e) {
    as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients) %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column("Predictor") %>%
      beautify_labels() %>% kill_scipen()
  })
}
```
