``` {r prep-functions}
# ==============================================================================
# 3. Data Loading & Cleaning
# ==============================================================================

standardize_id <- function(ids) {
  sprintf("Vp%04d", as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(ids, "\\d+")))
}

# Covariate loader. Retains raw (un-Z-scored) trait values; Stage 2 standardization
# happens inside the Stage 2 function where scoping is unambiguous.
load_covariates <- function(path_cov) {
  if (is.na(path_cov) || !file.exists(path_cov)) {
    warning("Covariate file unavailable; Stage 2 will be skipped.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  cat(sprintf("[Covariates] Loading: %s\n", basename(path_cov)))
  
  df_cov <- if (grepl("\\.csv$", path_cov)) {
    readr::read_csv(path_cov, show_col_types = FALSE)
  } else {
    readxl::read_excel(path_cov)
  }
  
  names(df_cov)[1] <- "raw_id"
  df_cov$participant_id <- standardize_id(df_cov$raw_id)
  
  df_cov_clean <- df_cov %>%
    dplyr::select(participant_id, dplyr::any_of(c("SVO_type", stage2_traits)))
  
  cat(sprintf("[Covariates] N = %d subjects, %d traits available.\n",
              nrow(df_cov_clean),
              sum(stage2_traits %in% names(df_cov_clean))))
  df_cov_clean
}

# ERP component loader and cleaner.
#
# Baseline preprocessing: mean-centered (NOT z-scored). Per Alday (2019), keeping
# baseline in microvolt units allows direct comparison with the published
# coefficient plots (Fig. 10) and preserves interpretation of beta_baseline as
# 'fraction of pre-stimulus drift propagated forward'.
#
# Outlier filter |amplitude| < 200 microvolts: in the Alday baseline-as-covariate
# framework, extreme target-window values often arise from baseline drift that
# the model can absorb. This filter is therefore conservative; the number of
# trimmed trials is logged for the manuscript Methods section.
load_and_prep <- function(path_erp, df_covariates, erp_name, baseline_col) {
  if (!file.exists(path_erp)) {
    stop(sprintf("ERP file missing: %s", path_erp))
  }
  
  df <- readr::read_csv(path_erp, show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  required_cols <- c("participant_id", "Offers_Other", "emotion", "index")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(df))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(sprintf("Required columns missing from %s: %s",
                 basename(path_erp), paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  
  if (!(erp_name %in% names(df))) {
    cat(sprintf("[SKIP] Component '%s' absent from data.\n", erp_name))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  df$participant_id <- standardize_id(df$participant_id)
  
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(Offers_Other %in% c(5, 6, 8, 9)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      offer_type = factor(
        dplyr::case_when(
          Offers_Other %in% c(5, 6) ~ "fair",
          Offers_Other %in% c(8, 9) ~ "unfair"
        ),
        levels = c("fair", "unfair")
      ),
      emotion = factor(emotion, levels = c("neu", "aff", "dis", "dom", "enj"))
    )
  
  orig_n <- nrow(df)
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(abs(.data[[erp_name]]) < 200)
  if (orig_n > nrow(df)) {
    cat(sprintf("[QC] %s: removed %d trials with |amplitude| > 200 \u00B5V (%.1f%%).\n",
                erp_name, orig_n - nrow(df), 100 * (orig_n - nrow(df)) / orig_n))
  }
  
  if (!is.null(baseline_col) && baseline_col %in% names(df)) {
    df$Baseline_Raw <- df[[baseline_col]]
    df$Baseline_c   <- df$Baseline_Raw - mean(df$Baseline_Raw, na.rm = TRUE)
    df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(Baseline_c))
  } else {
    # v2: strict failure on missing baseline column. Earlier versions silently
    # set Baseline_c = 0 ('no baseline correction'), which would alter the
    # Alday fixed-effect specification without notification. The Alday
    # framework requires baseline as a fitted covariate; if the column is
    # missing, the upstream extraction pipeline failed and the analysis must
    # be rerun, not silently degraded to a different model.
    stop(sprintf(
      paste("Baseline column '%s' missing from %s.",
            "Alday baseline-as-covariate framework requires this column.",
            "Re-run preprocessing with use_baseline_correction = FALSE",
            "and the matching baseline component in the extraction config.",
            sep = " "),
      baseline_col, basename(path_erp)
    ))
  }
  
  if (!is.null(df_covariates)) {
    df <- dplyr::left_join(df, df_covariates, by = "participant_id")
  }
  
  df
}

check_uniqueness <- function(df, context_name) {
  if (nrow(df) != dplyr::n_distinct(dplyr::select(df, participant_id, index))) {
    stop(sprintf("CRITICAL: duplicate (participant_id, index) keys in %s.", context_name))
  }
}

# Baseline pre-check: tests whether mean baseline differs across emotion x
# offer_type cells. Pure diagnostic. Does NOT gate the main analysis -- the
# Alday framework explicitly allows baseline-condition interactions and the
# main pipeline tests those interactions via LRT in fit_stage1_bates. This
# helper exists to:
#   (a) flag potential confounds for transparency in the Methods paragraph;
#   (b) provide a single number (omnibus interaction F) to cite when
#       reviewers ask "was baseline balanced across conditions?".
# Output written to Supplementary/baseline_balance/<component>.md.
# 
# Implementation note: uses the same LMM machinery as the main analysis
# (lmer + Type III F via Satterthwaite cascade) for methodological
# consistency. Each call adds ~10-30 seconds to runtime; total overhead
# across all components is < 3 minutes, negligible vs the Bates pipeline
# itself.
pre_check_baseline_balance <- function(data, comp_name, out_dir) {
  if (!"Baseline_c" %in% names(data)) {
    cat(sprintf("[PreCheck] %s: Baseline_c absent; skipping balance check.\n",
                comp_name))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  out_path <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("%s_baseline_balance.md", comp_name))
  
  cat(sprintf("[PreCheck] %s: testing baseline ~ emotion * offer_type ...\n",
              comp_name))
  
  fit <- tryCatch({
    bf <- lmerTest::lmer(
      Baseline_c ~ emotion * offer_type + (1 | participant_id),
      data = data, REML = TRUE
    )
    bf
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[PreCheck] %s: model failed (%s).\n",
                comp_name, conditionMessage(e)))
    NULL
  })
  if (is.null(fit)) return(invisible(NULL))
  
  # Class upgrade defensive (lmerTest::lmer should already produce
  # lmerModLmerTest, but check for safety).
  if (!inherits(fit, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
    fit <- tryCatch(lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(fit), error = function(e) fit)
  }
  
  res <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(anova(fit, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite")),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(res) || !any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
    res <- tryCatch(
      suppressWarnings(anova(fit, type = 3, ddf = "Kenward-Roger")),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
  }
  if (is.null(res)) {
    res <- tryCatch(car::Anova(fit, type = 3, test.statistic = "F"),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
  }
  
  apa_tab <- if (!is.null(res)) format_anova_apa(res, model = fit) else NULL
  
  # Extract the omnibus emotion:offer_type p-value if present, for a
  # one-line summary.
  interaction_p <- if (!is.null(apa_tab)) {
    int_row <- apa_tab[apa_tab$Effect == "emotion:offer_type", , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(int_row) == 1) int_row$p_val else NA_real_
  } else NA_real_
  
  cell_means <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(emotion, offer_type) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      mean_baseline = mean(Baseline_c, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_baseline   = sd(Baseline_c, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_trials      = dplyr::n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  writeLines(c(
    sprintf("# Baseline Balance Pre-Check: %s", comp_name),
    sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
    "",
    "## Purpose",
    "Diagnostic test of whether mean baseline amplitude differs across",
    "emotion x offer_type cells. PURE DIAGNOSTIC: does NOT gate or modify",
    "the main analysis. The Alday baseline-as-covariate framework allows",
    "baseline-condition interactions and tests them in the main model.",
    "",
    "## Test",
    "Model: Baseline_c ~ emotion * offer_type + (1 | participant_id)",
    "",
    if (!is.na(interaction_p)) {
      sprintf("Omnibus emotion:offer_type interaction: p = %s",
              if (interaction_p < .001) "< .001"
              else sprintf("%.3f", interaction_p))
    } else "Omnibus interaction: not extractable",
    "",
    "## Type III ANOVA",
    if (!is.null(apa_tab)) {
      knitr::kable(apa_tab, format = "markdown", row.names = FALSE)
    } else "Test failed.",
    "",
    "## Cell means (microvolts)",
    knitr::kable(cell_means, format = "markdown", digits = 3, row.names = FALSE),
    "",
    "## Interpretation",
    "If interaction p > 0.05: baseline is balanced across conditions; no",
    "concern. If p < 0.05: condition-dependent baseline detected. The main",
    "analysis tests Baseline_c:emotion and Baseline_c:offer_type",
    "interactions in fit_stage1_bates Step 3 (LRT-based inclusion); a",
    "significant baseline-condition coupling will be retained automatically",
    "in the final model and reported in REPRODUCIBILITY.txt."
  ), out_path)
  
  invisible(out_path)
}
```

``` {r bates-engine}
# ==============================================================================
# 4. Stage 1 Engine: Bates (2015) Five-Step Random-Structure Selection
#    Combined with Alday (2019) baseline-as-covariate fixed-effect specification.
# ==============================================================================
#
# FIXED-EFFECT SPECIFICATION (Alday Tier 2.5)
# Pairwise interactions among emotion, offer_type, and Baseline_c serve as the
# search space. The buildmer 'include' argument forces retention of theoretically
# core terms (emotion, offer_type, Baseline_c, emotion:offer_type); baseline-by-
# condition interactions are subjected to LRT-based inclusion testing. This is
# data-driven Alday: the pairwise specification is a hypothesis space rather
# than a commitment, and the final fixed structure may differ across experiments
# reflecting genuine differences in baseline-condition coupling.
#
# RANDOM-EFFECT STRUCTURE (Bates 2015 / Matuschek 2017 five-step pipeline)
#   Step 1: Design-justified maximal model with main-effect random slopes and
#           full correlation parameters. Interaction random slopes are omitted
#           because cell-level variance components rarely identify in single-
#           trial EEG data with typical N (50 subjects x 30 trials/cell).
#   Step 2: Zero-correlation-parameter (ZCP) model as fallback starting point
#           for variance-component selection.
#   Step 3: LRT-based backward elimination via buildmer (alpha = 0.20 per
#           Matuschek et al. 2017, equivalent to AIC for nested two-model
#           comparisons; avoids the over-conservative model selection that
#           strict alpha = 0.05 would impose at this stage).
#   Step 4: Test whether adding correlation parameters improves fit, by
#           enumerating candidate correlated structures over the surviving
#           variance components and selecting via LRT/AIC.
#   Step 5: rePCA diagnostic on the final model documents the dimensionality
#           supported by the data, written to the reproducibility log.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: parse a fitted model's formula to identify which random slopes
# survived Step 3. Returns a character vector of slope variable names.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
extract_surviving_slopes <- function(model) {
  re_terms <- lme4::findbars(formula(model))
  surviving <- character(0)
  for (term in re_terms) {
    rhs <- deparse(term[[2]])
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*0\\s*\\+\\s*", "", rhs)
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*1\\s*\\+\\s*", "", rhs)
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*1\\s*$",       "", rhs)
    rhs <- trimws(rhs)
    if (rhs == "" || rhs == "1") next
    parts <- trimws(strsplit(rhs, "\\+")[[1]])
    surviving <- c(surviving, parts)
  }
  unique(surviving)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: rePCA dimensionality summary as a tidy data frame, one row per
# principal component with cumulative variance explained.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
extract_repca_summary <- function(model, group_name = "participant_id") {
  # Defensive: rePCA() requires a merMod object; lm or lmerTest objects without
  # the underlying lme4 slot will trigger getME() failures. Return an NA frame
  # so downstream count_effective_dims() returns NA cleanly.
  if (!inherits(model, "merMod")) {
    return(data.frame(component = NA_integer_, sd = NA_real_,
                      proportion_variance = NA_real_,
                      cumulative_variance = NA_real_))
  }
  pca_obj <- tryCatch(lme4::rePCA(model), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(pca_obj) || !group_name %in% names(pca_obj)) {
    return(data.frame(component = NA_integer_, sd = NA_real_,
                      proportion_variance = NA_real_,
                      cumulative_variance = NA_real_))
  }
  imp <- summary(pca_obj[[group_name]])$importance
  data.frame(
    component = seq_len(ncol(imp)),
    sd = imp["Standard deviation", ],
    proportion_variance = imp["Proportion of Variance", ],
    cumulative_variance = imp["Cumulative Proportion", ]
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: count effective dimensions (those reaching >= threshold cumulative
# variance). Indicates whether the random structure is overparameterized.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
count_effective_dims <- function(repca_df, threshold = 0.999) {
  if (all(is.na(repca_df$cumulative_variance))) return(NA_integer_)
  hit <- which(repca_df$cumulative_variance >= threshold)
  if (length(hit) == 0) nrow(repca_df) else hit[1]
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 4 helper: enumerate candidate correlated structures over surviving
# variance components, fit each, and select via LRT vs. ZCP (alpha = 0.20 per
# Matuschek et al. 2017). Returns the best-fitting model with REML refitted
# for inference.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_correlations_step4 <- function(model_zcp_reduced, fixed_str, data, alpha_lrt = 0.20) {
  # Defensive: if the reduced model is not an lme4 mixed model (e.g. degraded
  # to plain lm during Step 3), there are no random slopes to add correlations
  # to. Return as-is.
  if (!inherits(model_zcp_reduced, "merMod")) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] Reduced model is not a mixed model; skipping correlation tests.",
                 indent = 1)
    return(model_zcp_reduced)
  }
  
  surviving <- extract_surviving_slopes(model_zcp_reduced)
  
  if (length(surviving) == 0) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] Reduced model has only random intercept; no correlations to test.",
                 indent = 1)
    # SAFETY: do NOT use update(model_zcp_reduced, REML = TRUE). When
    # model_zcp_reduced was extracted from buildmer (bm_res@model), its
    # @call slot stores buildmer's internal data placeholder ('..2'),
    # not the actual data argument. update.merMod tries to re-evaluate
    # the call in the current environment, where '..2' does not exist,
    # producing "bad 'data': ..2 used in an incorrect context".
    # Explicit refit using formula(model) and the function's `data`
    # argument bypasses this issue.
    f_zcp_only <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
    return(lme4::lmer(f_zcp_only, data = data, REML = TRUE,
                      control = custom_control))
  }
  
  # Build candidate set. ZCP-baseline always included for LRT baseline.
  candidates <- list()
  candidates[["ZCP_baseline"]] <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
  
  # All-correlated candidate: (1 + s1 + s2 + ... | id)
  all_str <- paste(surviving, collapse = " + ")
  candidates[["All_correlated"]] <- as.formula(
    paste(fixed_str, "+ (1 +", all_str, "| participant_id)")
  )
  
  # Pairwise candidates: intercept correlated with one slope at a time.
  if (length(surviving) > 1) {
    for (i in seq_along(surviving)) {
      others <- setdiff(surviving, surviving[i])
      if (length(others) > 0) {
        others_terms <- paste(
          sprintf("(0 + %s | participant_id)", others),
          collapse = " + "
        )
        cand_str <- paste(fixed_str,
                          sprintf("+ (1 + %s | participant_id)", surviving[i]),
                          "+", others_terms)
      } else {
        cand_str <- paste(fixed_str,
                          sprintf("+ (1 + %s | participant_id)", surviving[i]))
      }
      candidates[[paste0("Int_with_", surviving[i])]] <- as.formula(cand_str)
    }
  }
  
  # Fit each candidate under ML for valid LRT comparison.
  total_cands <- length(candidates)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] Fitting %d candidate correlated structures...",
                       total_cands), indent = 1)
  fits <- list()
  cand_idx <- 0
  for (nm in names(candidates)) {
    cand_idx <- cand_idx + 1
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] Trying '%s'...",
                         cand_idx, total_cands, nm), indent = 2)
    t_cand <- Sys.time()
    fit <- tryCatch(
      lme4::lmer(candidates[[nm]], data = data, REML = FALSE, control = custom_control),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (!is.null(fit) && !lme4::isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-4)) {
      fits[[nm]] <- fit
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' converged (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    } else if (!is.null(fit)) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' singular; excluded (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    } else {
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' failed to converge (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    }
  }
  
  if (length(fits) == 0) {
    # All candidates were singular or failed. Per Bates (2015), this means the
    # data does not support any random-slope variance components beyond the
    # intercept. Refit with random-intercept-only structure.
    progress_log("[Step 4] All candidates singular; data does not support random slopes.",
                 indent = 1)
    progress_log("[Step 4] Refitting with random-intercept-only structure.", indent = 2)
    
    fixed_only_part <- nobars(formula(model_zcp_reduced))
    f_min <- as.formula(paste(deparse(fixed_only_part), "+ (1 | participant_id)"))
    m_min <- lme4::lmer(f_min, data = data, REML = TRUE, control = custom_control)
    attr(m_min, "step4_selected") <- "RandomIntercept_only"
    return(m_min)
  }
  
  if (length(fits) == 1) {
    # Only ZCP_baseline survived (others singular). Keep it.
    progress_log("[Step 4] Only ZCP candidate viable; correlations not added.", indent = 1)
    # See safety note above re: update() and buildmer-derived models.
    f_zcp_only <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
    return(lme4::lmer(f_zcp_only, data = data, REML = TRUE,
                      control = custom_control))
  }
  
  # Establish a working reference for LRT comparisons. ZCP_baseline (the simplest
  # candidate, no correlations) is the preferred reference because all richer
  # candidates are nested within it. If it failed to converge but other candidates
  # succeeded, fall back to selecting by AIC alone.
  # NOTE: "baseline" here refers to the Step 4 reference model, NOT to the
  # pre-stimulus EEG baseline (Baseline_c). The two are unrelated.
  baseline_fit <- fits[["ZCP_baseline"]]
  lrt_table <- data.frame(model = character(), df_diff = integer(),
                          chisq = numeric(), p_value = numeric(),
                          AIC = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  if (is.null(baseline_fit)) {
    # ZCP_baseline was singular but at least one alternative converged.
    # Select the candidate with lowest AIC.
    progress_log("[Step 4] ZCP_baseline singular; selecting best converged candidate by AIC.",
                 indent = 1)
    aics <- sapply(fits, AIC)
    best_name <- names(fits)[which.min(aics)]
    best_fit  <- fits[[best_name]]
    
    for (nm in names(fits)) {
      lrt_table <- rbind(lrt_table, data.frame(
        model = nm,
        df_diff = NA_integer_,
        chisq = NA_real_,
        p_value = NA_real_,
        AIC = aics[nm],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
    }
  } else {
    # Standard path: ZCP_baseline available, perform nested LRTs against it.
    best_name <- "ZCP_baseline"
    best_fit  <- baseline_fit
    
    for (nm in setdiff(names(fits), "ZCP_baseline")) {
      cand <- fits[[nm]]
      lrt <- tryCatch(anova(baseline_fit, cand), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(lrt) || nrow(lrt) < 2) next
      
      p_val <- lrt$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2]
      if (is.na(p_val)) next
      
      lrt_table <- rbind(lrt_table, data.frame(
        model = nm,
        df_diff = lrt$Df[2],
        chisq = lrt$Chisq[2],
        p_value = p_val,
        AIC = AIC(cand),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
      
      # Select candidate with lowest AIC among those passing alpha_lrt.
      if (p_val < alpha_lrt && AIC(cand) < AIC(best_fit)) {
        best_name <- nm
        best_fit  <- cand
      }
    }
  }
  
  attr(best_fit, "step4_lrt_table") <- lrt_table
  attr(best_fit, "step4_selected") <- best_name
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] Selected: %s (alpha_LRT = %.2f).",
                       best_name, alpha_lrt), indent = 1)
  
  update(best_fit, REML = TRUE)
}

# ==============================================================================
# Main Stage 1 engine: full Bates 5-step pipeline + Alday 2.5 fixed structure.
# Returns the fitted model with diagnostic attributes attached.
# ==============================================================================
fit_stage1_bates <- function(data, erp_name) {
  
  fixed_str <- sprintf("%s ~ (emotion + offer_type + Baseline_c)^2", erp_name)
  
  # Forced-include set for buildmer Step 3: theoretical core terms that must
  # remain regardless of LRT outcome. The by-subject random intercept is also
  # forced to remain because it reflects the nested data structure (trials
  # within subjects); without it, single-trial EEG data are pseudo-replicated
  # and inferential statistics are invalid. Baseline interactions are NOT in
  # this set, allowing the data to decide whether they are supported.
  fixed_include <- as.formula(
    "~ emotion + offer_type + Baseline_c + emotion:offer_type + (1 | participant_id)"
  )
  
  diag_log <- list(
    component = erp_name,
    n_obs = nrow(data),
    n_subjects = dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id),
    step1_status = NA_character_,
    step1_pca = NULL,
    step2_status = NA_character_,
    step3_final_formula = NA_character_,
    step4_status = NA_character_,
    step5_pca = NULL
  )
  
  # ---- STEP 1: Barr-style maximal model (main-effects random slopes only). ----
  progress_log(sprintf("[%s] Stage 1: Bates 5-step random-structure selection",
                       erp_name))
  progress_log(sprintf("Data: N = %d trials, %d subjects.",
                       nrow(data), dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id)),
               indent = 1)
  
  random_max <- "(1 + emotion + offer_type | participant_id)"
  f_max <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+", random_max))
  
  progress_log("[Step 1] Fitting design-justified maximal model with correlations...",
               indent = 1)
  t_step1 <- Sys.time()
  m_max <- tryCatch(
    lme4::lmer(f_max, data = data, REML = FALSE, control = custom_control),
    error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[ERROR] Maximal fit failed: %s", conditionMessage(e)),
                   indent = 2)
      NULL
    }
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 1] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step1)),
               indent = 2)
  
  if (!is.null(m_max)) {
    is_sing <- lme4::isSingular(m_max, tol = 1e-4)
    diag_log$step1_status <- if (is_sing) "converged_singular" else "converged_clean"
    diag_log$step1_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_max)
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 1] Status: %s. Effective dims = %d / %d.",
                         diag_log$step1_status,
                         count_effective_dims(diag_log$step1_pca),
                         nrow(diag_log$step1_pca)),
                 indent = 2)
  } else {
    diag_log$step1_status <- "failed_to_converge"
  }
  
  # ---- STEP 2: Zero-correlation-parameter (ZCP) model. ----
  progress_log("[Step 2] Fitting zero-correlation-parameter model...", indent = 1)
  t_step2 <- Sys.time()
  
  random_zcp <- paste("(1 | participant_id)",
                      "(0 + emotion | participant_id)",
                      "(0 + offer_type | participant_id)",
                      sep = " + ")
  f_zcp <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+", random_zcp))
  
  m_zcp <- tryCatch(
    lme4::lmer(f_zcp, data = data, REML = FALSE, control = custom_control),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 2] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step2)), indent = 2)
  
  if (is.null(m_zcp)) {
    progress_log("[Step 2] [ERROR] ZCP fit failed; falling back to random-intercept-only.",
                 indent = 2)
    diag_log$step2_status <- "failed"
    f_minimal <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+ (1 | participant_id)"))
    m_zcp <- lme4::lmer(f_minimal, data = data, REML = FALSE, control = custom_control)
  } else {
    is_sing_zcp <- lme4::isSingular(m_zcp, tol = 1e-4)
    diag_log$step2_status <- if (is_sing_zcp) "converged_singular" else "converged_clean"
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 2] Status: %s.", diag_log$step2_status), indent = 2)
  }
  
  # ---- STEP 3: LRT-based backward elimination via buildmer. ----
  # buildmer drops both fixed-effect baseline interactions and random-effect
  # variance components if not supported by data. Theoretical core terms are
  # protected by the 'include' argument.
  #
  # Elimination criterion uses alpha = 0.20 per Matuschek, Kliegl, Vasishth,
  # Baayen, & Bates (2017, Journal of Memory and Language). Their simulations
  # showed that alpha = 0.05 over-penalizes model complexity at the elimination
  # stage, sacrificing power to detect true fixed effects. Alpha = 0.20 is
  # approximately equivalent to AIC-based selection for nested two-model
  # comparisons and provides the optimal Type I error / power tradeoff for
  # typical psychological / psycholinguistic datasets.
  #
  # Note on buildmer API: 'crit' governs term ordering (default LRT), while
  # 'elim' governs elimination decisions. LRTalpha() generates an elimination
  # function and must be passed to 'elim', not 'crit'.
  progress_log("[Step 3] LRT-based backward elimination (buildmer, alpha = 0.20)...",
               indent = 1)
  progress_log(paste("This step iteratively tests model terms via LRT and may fit",
                     "many candidate models. With large N (>20,000 trials) and",
                     "complex random structures, expect several minutes per",
                     "component. buildmer's internal progress is shown below."),
               indent = 2)
  progress_log("[Step 3] Engineering protections active: lmerTest detached during",
               indent = 2)
  progress_log("buildmer call; withTimeout=1800s; ZCP fallback on failure.",
               indent = 2)
  t_step3 <- Sys.time()
  
  bm_ctrl <- buildmer::buildmerControl(
    include = fixed_include,
    direction = c("order", "backward"),
    crit = "LRT",
    elim = buildmer::LRTalpha(0.20),
    quiet = FALSE,
    args = list(control = custom_control)
    # Note: REML is managed by buildmer internally based on whether the
    # comparison is between fixed-effect or random-effect changes. Passing
    # REML here causes a duplicate-argument error.
  )
  
  bm_res <- run_buildmer_protected(
    buildmer::buildmer,
    formula = f_zcp, data = data,
    buildmerControl = bm_ctrl,
    timeout_sec = 1800
  )
  
  if (is.null(bm_res)) {
    progress_log("[Step 3] buildmer failed or timed out; retaining ZCP model.",
                 indent = 2)
    m_reduced <- m_zcp
  } else {
    m_reduced <- tryCatch({
      bm_res@model
    }, error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[WARN] Could not extract @model: %s; retaining ZCP.",
                           conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
      m_zcp
    })
  }
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 3] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step3)), indent = 2)
  
  # Sanity check: buildmer can occasionally eliminate ALL random-effect terms,
  # returning a plain `lm` object. Single-trial EEG analysis without random
  # intercepts is invalid (pseudo-replication of trials within subjects), so we
  # rebuild the minimum viable LMM with a random intercept. This branch should
  # be rare given that (1 | participant_id) is in the include set above.
  if (!inherits(m_reduced, "merMod")) {
    progress_log("[WARN] Reduced model lost all random effects; refitting with (1 | participant_id).",
                 indent = 2)
    reduced_fixed_str_recovered <- paste(deparse(formula(m_reduced)), collapse = " ")
    f_recover <- as.formula(paste(reduced_fixed_str_recovered, "+ (1 | participant_id)"))
    m_reduced <- lme4::lmer(f_recover, data = data, REML = FALSE,
                            control = custom_control)
  }
  
  diag_log$step3_final_formula <- paste(deparse(formula(m_reduced)), collapse = " ")
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 3] Reduced formula: %s",
                       stringr::str_squish(diag_log$step3_final_formula)),
               indent = 2)
  
  # ---- STEP 4: Test correlation parameters on surviving slopes. ----
  progress_log("[Step 4] Testing correlation parameters on surviving slopes...",
               indent = 1)
  t_step4 <- Sys.time()
  
  # Reconstruct fixed-only formula from the reduced model for Step 4 candidates.
  reduced_fixed <- nobars(formula(m_reduced))
  reduced_fixed_str <- paste(deparse(reduced_fixed), collapse = " ")
  
  m_final <- add_correlations_step4(m_reduced, reduced_fixed_str, data, alpha_lrt = 0.20)
  diag_log$step4_status <- attr(m_final, "step4_selected") %||% "ZCP_kept"
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] elapsed: %s. Selected: %s.",
                       format_elapsed(t_step4), diag_log$step4_status),
               indent = 2)
  
  # ---- STEP 5: rePCA diagnostic on final model. ----
  diag_log$step5_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_final)
  step5_eff <- count_effective_dims(diag_log$step5_pca)
  step5_nom <- nrow(diag_log$step5_pca)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 5] Final model dimensionality: %s effective / %s nominal.",
                       if (is.na(step5_eff)) "NA" else as.character(step5_eff),
                       if (is.na(step5_nom)) "NA" else as.character(step5_nom)),
               indent = 1)
  
  # ---- Defensive REML guard. ----
  # 
  # Several paths through add_correlations_step4 and fit_stage1_bates can
  # return an LMM in ML state (REML=FALSE). lmerTest::anova(ddf="Satterthwaite")
  # expects REML by default. Refit REML here unconditionally so the downstream
  # ANOVA cascade has a clean input.
  # 
  # SAFETY: do NOT use update() because m_final may be a buildmer @model
  # object whose @call references buildmer's internal '..2' placeholder,
  # which fails outside buildmer's scope. Refit explicitly from formula
  # and the local `data` argument.
  if (inherits(m_final, "merMod")) {
    is_reml <- tryCatch(lme4::isREML(m_final), error = function(e) FALSE)
    if (!isTRUE(is_reml)) {
      progress_log("[Final] Refitting LMM with REML=TRUE for Satterthwaite compatibility.",
                   indent = 1)
      f_final <- formula(m_final)
      m_final_reml <- tryCatch(
        lme4::lmer(f_final, data = data, REML = TRUE, control = custom_control),
        error = function(e) {
          progress_log(sprintf("[Final] REML refit failed: %s; retaining ML fit.",
                               conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
          NULL
        }
      )
      if (!is.null(m_final_reml)) {
        existing_attrs <- attributes(m_final)[c("step4_selected",
                                                "step4_lrt_table")]
        for (an in names(existing_attrs)) {
          if (!is.null(existing_attrs[[an]])) {
            attr(m_final_reml, an) <- existing_attrs[[an]]
          }
        }
        m_final <- m_final_reml
      }
    }
  }
  
  # ---- Defensive lmerTest class upgrade. ----
  # 
  # CRITICAL for Satterthwaite/KR p-values. When fit via lme4::lmer() (rather
  # than lmerTest::lmer()), the resulting object has class "lmerMod" only.
  # Calling anova(model, ddf="Satterthwaite") on a bare lmerMod does NOT
  # dispatch to lmerTest's S4 method; lme4's base anova() handles it,
  # silently ignoring the ddf argument and returning a table with F values
  # but NO Pr(>F) and NO NumDF/DenDF columns. The downstream cascade then
  # detects "no Pr column" and falls through to Wald.
  # 
  # The fix is to upgrade the class via lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest() (a
  # free no-refit operation that registers the model with lmerTest's
  # df-computation machinery). buildmer internally fits via lmerTest::lmer()
  # so its @model output may already be lmerModLmerTest; but our 
  # add_correlations_step4 refits via lme4::lmer() in many paths, losing the
  # lmerTest class. This guard ensures the final returned model is dispatch-
  # ready regardless of which fallback path was taken.
  if (inherits(m_final, "merMod") && !inherits(m_final, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
    m_final_lt <- tryCatch(
      lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(m_final),
      error = function(e) {
        progress_log(sprintf("[Final] lmerTest class upgrade failed: %s",
                             conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (!is.null(m_final_lt)) {
      existing_attrs <- attributes(m_final)[c("step4_selected",
                                              "step4_lrt_table")]
      for (an in names(existing_attrs)) {
        if (!is.null(existing_attrs[[an]])) {
          attr(m_final_lt, an) <- existing_attrs[[an]]
        }
      }
      m_final <- m_final_lt
      progress_log("[Final] LMM upgraded to lmerModLmerTest for Satt/KR dispatch.",
                   indent = 1)
    }
  }
  
  attr(m_final, "bates_diag") <- diag_log
  m_final
}
```


``` {r stage1-runner}
# ==============================================================================
# 5. Stage 1 Runner: fit, decompose, and report for one ERP component.
#    Replaces the original run_regression_analysis function.
# ==============================================================================
run_stage1_component <- function(data, erp_name, out_dir, exp_version) {
  
  comp_dir <- file.path(out_dir, erp_name)
  if (!dir.exists(comp_dir)) dir.create(comp_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  
  progress_log(sprintf(">>> Component: %s [%s] (N_subj = %d, N_trial = %d)",
                       erp_name, exp_version,
                       dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id), nrow(data)))
  
  # ---- Fit Stage 1 model via Bates 5-step pipeline. ----
  FINAL_MODEL <- fit_stage1_bates(data, erp_name)
  diag_log <- attr(FINAL_MODEL, "bates_diag")
  
  formula_str <- paste(deparse(formula(FINAL_MODEL)), collapse = " ")
  progress_log(sprintf("[Final model] %s", stringr::str_squish(formula_str)), indent = 1)
  
  # ---- Type III ANOVA: cascade Satterthwaite -> Kenward-Roger -> Wald. ----
  # 
  # CASCADE: lmerTest cascade for LMM.
  #   (1) Satterthwaite F  - lmerTest::anova; preferred (Luke 2017).
  #   (2) Kenward-Roger F  - pbkrtest backend; conservative fallback,
  #       different numerical implementation than Satterthwaite.
  #   (3) Wald chi-square  - car::Anova; last resort, asymptotic.
  # 
  # The cascade is necessary because lmerTest's Satt/KR dispatch requires
  # the model to have class "lmerModLmerTest" (not bare "lmerMod"). The
  # fit_stage1_bates engine upgrades the class before returning, but a
  # second defensive upgrade here protects against models loaded from
  # disk via readRDS or any other path bypassing the engine guard.
  progress_log("[ANOVA] Computing Type III tests...", indent = 1)
  t_anova <- Sys.time()
  
  # Defensive class upgrade. See fit_stage1_bates for full rationale.
  if (inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "merMod") &&
      !inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
    FINAL_MODEL_lt <- tryCatch(
      lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(FINAL_MODEL),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (!is.null(FINAL_MODEL_lt)) FINAL_MODEL <- FINAL_MODEL_lt
  }
  
  anova_res <- NULL
  method_used <- NA_character_
  
  # Attempt 1: Satterthwaite.
  anova_res <- tryCatch({
    res <- suppressWarnings(anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
    if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
      method_used <- "Satterthwaite_F"
      res
    } else {
      progress_log("[ANOVA] Satterthwaite returned no p-value column; trying Kenward-Roger.",
                   indent = 2)
      NULL
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] Satterthwaite errored (%s); trying Kenward-Roger.",
                         conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
    NULL
  })
  
  # Attempt 2: Kenward-Roger.
  if (is.null(anova_res)) {
    anova_res <- tryCatch({
      res <- suppressWarnings(anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, ddf = "Kenward-Roger"))
      if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
        method_used <- "Kenward_Roger_F"
        res
      } else {
        progress_log("[ANOVA] Kenward-Roger returned no p-value column; falling back to Wald.",
                     indent = 2)
        NULL
      }
    }, error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] Kenward-Roger errored (%s); falling back to Wald.",
                           conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
      NULL
    })
  }
  
  # Attempt 3: Wald.
  if (is.null(anova_res)) {
    anova_res <- car::Anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, test.statistic = "Chisq")
    method_used <- "Wald_chi_square"
  }
  
  diag_log$anova_method <- method_used
  progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] Method: %s. Elapsed: %s.",
                       method_used, format_elapsed(t_anova)),
               indent = 2)
  
  anova_apa <- format_anova_apa(anova_res, FINAL_MODEL)
  # Include partial eta-squared with 95% CI in console print so users see
  # effect sizes during long pipeline runs. The full table (with p_val
  # column) is written to anova_apa.md; controlling print width avoids
  # console wrapping.
  print(anova_apa %>% dplyr::select(Effect, APA_Report, eta2_partial_95CI, Sig))
  
  # ---- Post-hoc decomposition. ----
  # 
  # Two-tier gating (v2):
  #   p_int < confirmatory_alpha (0.05): simple-effect contrasts go to
  #     main reporting tables (Confirmatory).
  #   confirmatory_alpha <= p_int < marginal_threshold (0.10): contrasts
  #     are computed and labeled Exploratory_Marginal; written to the
  #     Supplementary directory but NOT to the main tables.
  #   p_int >= marginal_threshold: no simple-effect extraction.
  # Main effects are reported regardless, for transparency.
  cat("   [Post-hoc] FDR-corrected within family...\n")
  
  # Extract interaction p-value defensively. Different anova() implementations
  # return p-values under different column names ('Pr(>F)' for lmerTest,
  # 'Pr(>Chisq)' for car::Anova).
  target_2way <- "emotion:offer_type"
  p_int_2way <- NA_real_
  if (target_2way %in% rownames(anova_res)) {
    p_candidates <- c("Pr(>F)", "Pr(>Chisq)")
    for (pcol in p_candidates) {
      if (pcol %in% colnames(anova_res)) {
        val <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(anova_res[target_2way, pcol]))
        if (length(val) == 1 && !is.na(val)) {
          p_int_2way <- val
          break
        }
      }
    }
  }
  if (is.na(p_int_2way)) p_int_2way <- 1.0
  
  at_list <- list(Baseline_c = 0)
  
  # Helper: emmeans pairs/contrast with explicit infer=c(TRUE,TRUE) so that
  # summary() returns BOTH lower.CL/upper.CL columns AND p.value column.
  # Default behavior of pairs() returns only one or the other depending on
  # context; format_posthoc_apa requires both.
  pairs_with_ci <- function(emm, ...) {
    summary(pairs(emm, ...), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
  }
  contrast_with_ci <- function(emm, ...) {
    summary(contrast(emm, ...), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
  }
  
  list_of_tables <- list(
    "ANOVA_Main" = anova_apa,
    "Model_Formula" = data.frame(Formula = formula_str),
    "Model_Coefficients" = format_coefs(FINAL_MODEL)
  )
  list_of_supp_tables <- list()
  
  if (p_int_2way < marginal_threshold) {
    is_confirmatory <- (p_int_2way < confirmatory_alpha)
    status_tag <- if (is_confirmatory) "Confirmatory" else "Exploratory_Marginal"
    target_list <- if (is_confirmatory) "list_of_tables" else "list_of_supp_tables"
    
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc] Interaction p = %.4f -> %s simple effects.",
                         p_int_2way, status_tag), indent = 1)
    
    progress_log("[Post-hoc 1/3] offer_type | emotion (FDR)...", indent = 2)
    t_ph <- Sys.time()
    so_em <- format_posthoc_apa(
      pairs_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ offer_type | emotion, at = at_list),
                    adjust = "fdr")
    )
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc 1/3] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_ph)), indent = 3)
    so_em$Status <- status_tag
    if (is_confirmatory) list_of_tables[["Simple_Offer_by_Emotion"]] <- so_em
    else list_of_supp_tables[["MARGINAL_Simple_Offer_by_Emotion"]] <- so_em
    
    progress_log("[Post-hoc 2/3] emotion | offer_type (FDR)...", indent = 2)
    t_ph <- Sys.time()
    se_off <- format_posthoc_apa(
      pairs_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ emotion | offer_type, at = at_list),
                    adjust = "fdr")
    )
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc 2/3] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_ph)), indent = 3)
    se_off$Status <- status_tag
    if (is_confirmatory) list_of_tables[["Simple_Emotion_by_Offer"]] <- se_off
    else list_of_supp_tables[["MARGINAL_Simple_Emotion_by_Offer"]] <- se_off
    
    progress_log("[Post-hoc 3/3] interaction contrasts (FDR)...", indent = 2)
    t_ph <- Sys.time()
    int_contr <- format_posthoc_apa(
      contrast_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ emotion * offer_type, at = at_list),
                       interaction = "pairwise", adjust = "fdr")
    )
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc 3/3] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_ph)), indent = 3)
    int_contr$Status <- status_tag
    if (is_confirmatory) list_of_tables[["Interaction_Contrasts"]] <- int_contr
    else list_of_supp_tables[["MARGINAL_Interaction_Contrasts"]] <- int_contr
    
  } else {
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc] Interaction p = %.4f -> Reporting main effects only.",
                         p_int_2way), indent = 1)
  }
  
  progress_log("[Main effect] emotion pairwise (FDR)...", indent = 2)
  t_me <- Sys.time()
  list_of_tables[["Main_Effect_Emotion"]] <- format_posthoc_apa(
    pairs_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ emotion, at = at_list), adjust = "fdr")
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Main effect emotion] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_me)), indent = 3)
  
  progress_log("[Main effect] offer_type pairwise (Tukey)...", indent = 2)
  t_me <- Sys.time()
  list_of_tables[["Main_Effect_Offer"]] <- format_posthoc_apa(
    pairs_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ offer_type, at = at_list), adjust = "tukey")
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Main effect offer_type] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_me)), indent = 3)
  
  progress_log("[Descriptive] estimated marginal means...", indent = 2)
  t_me <- Sys.time()
  list_of_tables[["Descriptive_Means"]] <- beautify_labels(kill_scipen(
    as.data.frame(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ offer_type * emotion, at = at_list))
  ))
  progress_log(sprintf("[Descriptive] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_me)), indent = 3)
  
  # ---- Reporting Layer (replaces multi-sheet Excel as primary output). ----
  
  # Component status (confirmatory vs exploratory) for downstream filtering.
  comp_status <- component_status(erp_name)
  
  # 1. REPRODUCIBILITY metadata.
  sink(file.path(comp_dir, "REPRODUCIBILITY.txt"))
  cat("# Reproducibility log for ERP component:", erp_name, "\n")
  cat("# Generated:", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n\n")
  cat("## Status: ", comp_status, "\n\n")
  cat("## Final formula:\n")
  cat(formula_str, "\n\n")
  cat("## Software versions:\n")
  cat("R:        ", R.version.string, "\n")
  cat("lme4:     ", as.character(packageVersion("lme4")), "\n")
  cat("lmerTest: ", as.character(packageVersion("lmerTest")), "\n")
  cat("pbkrtest: ", as.character(packageVersion("pbkrtest")), "\n")
  cat("buildmer: ", as.character(packageVersion("buildmer")), "\n")
  cat("emmeans:  ", as.character(packageVersion("emmeans")), "\n\n")
  cat("## Convergence diagnostics:\n")
  cat("Optimizer:    bobyqa\n")
  cat("Singular fit:", lme4::isSingular(FINAL_MODEL, tol = 1e-4), "\n")
  cat("REML:         TRUE\n")
  cat("Observations:", nobs(FINAL_MODEL), "\n")
  cat("Subjects:    ", lme4::ngrps(FINAL_MODEL)["participant_id"], "\n\n")
  cat("## Bates 5-step diagnostic log:\n")
  cat("Term ordering criterion:     LRT (default)\n")
  cat("Term elimination criterion:  LRTalpha(0.20) (Matuschek et al., 2017)\n")
  cat("Step 1 (Maximal):           ", diag_log$step1_status, "\n")
  if (!is.null(diag_log$step1_pca)) {
    cat("  Step 1 effective/nominal: ",
        count_effective_dims(diag_log$step1_pca), "/",
        nrow(diag_log$step1_pca), "\n")
  }
  cat("Step 2 (ZCP):               ", diag_log$step2_status, "\n")
  cat("Step 3 (LRT reduction):     ", diag_log$step3_final_formula, "\n")
  cat("Step 4 (correlations):      ", diag_log$step4_status, "\n")
  cat("Step 5 (final dims):        ",
      count_effective_dims(diag_log$step5_pca), "/",
      nrow(diag_log$step5_pca), "\n")
  cat("\n## Inferential method:\n")
  cat("ANOVA test:                 ", diag_log$anova_method %||% "Wald_chi_square",
      "\n")
  if (identical(diag_log$anova_method, "Kenward_Roger_F")) {
    cat("Note: Satterthwaite returned no p-value column; Kenward-Roger\n")
    cat("(pbkrtest backend) used as second-tier method. Both Satt and KR\n")
    cat("are finite-DenDF F approximations; KR is more conservative.\n")
  }
  if (identical(diag_log$anova_method, "Wald_chi_square")) {
    cat("Note: Both Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger failed (no p-value\n")
    cat("column or error). Wald chi-square (car::Anova) used as final\n")
    cat("fallback. Wald is anti-conservative for finite N (Luke 2017),\n")
    cat("interpret reported p-values with caution.\n")
  }
  sink()
  
  # 2. saveRDS for offline re-analysis (Methods replication, sensitivity).
  saveRDS(FINAL_MODEL,
          file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("final_model_%s.rds", erp_name)))
  
  # 3. Full model summary (Alday-style transparency).
  sink(file.path(comp_dir, "summary_text.txt"))
  print(summary(FINAL_MODEL))
  sink()
  
  # 4. ANOVA table in markdown (manuscript-ready).
  writeLines(
    knitr::kable(anova_apa, format = "markdown",
                 caption = sprintf("Type III ANOVA (%s), %s.",
                                   diag_log$anova_method %||% "Wald", erp_name)),
    con = file.path(comp_dir, "anova_apa.md")
  )
  
  # 5. R-squared (Nakagawa & Schielzeth, 2013).
  r2_obj <- tryCatch(performance::r2(FINAL_MODEL), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(r2_obj)) {
    r2_df <- data.frame(
      R2_marginal    = r2_obj$R2_marginal,
      R2_conditional = r2_obj$R2_conditional
    )
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(kill_scipen(r2_df), format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Nakagawa & Schielzeth R\u00B2, %s.", erp_name)),
      con = file.path(comp_dir, "r2.md")
    )
  }
  
  # 6. Post-hoc tables in markdown (one file per contrast type).
  # Confirmatory tables go to comp_dir; marginal tables go to Supplementary.
  for (nm in names(list_of_tables)) {
    safe_nm <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", nm)
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(list_of_tables[[nm]], format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("%s -- %s", erp_name, nm)),
      con = file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("posthoc_%s.md", safe_nm))
    )
  }
  
  if (length(list_of_supp_tables) > 0) {
    supp_comp_dir <- file.path(out_suppl,
                               sprintf("%s_marginal_contrasts", erp_name))
    if (!dir.exists(supp_comp_dir)) dir.create(supp_comp_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    for (nm in names(list_of_supp_tables)) {
      safe_nm <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", nm)
      writeLines(
        knitr::kable(list_of_supp_tables[[nm]], format = "markdown",
                     caption = sprintf("%s -- %s [MARGINAL: 0.05<=p<0.10]",
                                       erp_name, nm)),
        con = file.path(supp_comp_dir, sprintf("posthoc_%s.md", safe_nm))
      )
    }
  }
  
  # 7. Step 4 LRT comparison table (when applicable).
  step4_lrt <- attr(FINAL_MODEL, "step4_lrt_table")
  if (!is.null(step4_lrt) && nrow(step4_lrt) > 0) {
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(kill_scipen(step4_lrt), format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Step 4 candidate-correlation LRT, %s.", erp_name)),
      con = file.path(comp_dir, "step4_correlation_lrt.md")
    )
  }
  
  # 8. Bates rePCA summary in markdown (Step 5 documentation).
  if (!is.null(diag_log$step5_pca) && !all(is.na(diag_log$step5_pca$component))) {
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(kill_scipen(diag_log$step5_pca), format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Final-model rePCA dimensionality, %s.", erp_name)),
      con = file.path(comp_dir, "step5_rePCA.md")
    )
  }
  
  # 9. Excel export (legacy compatibility for non-markdown workflows).
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  for (sheet_name in names(list_of_tables)) {
    safe_sheet <- substr(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", sheet_name), 1, 31)
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, safe_sheet)
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, safe_sheet, list_of_tables[[sheet_name]])
    openxlsx::addStyle(wb, safe_sheet,
      openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", border = "Bottom"),
      rows = 1, cols = 1:ncol(list_of_tables[[sheet_name]]))
  }
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb,
    file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("STATS_%s_%s.xlsx", exp_version, erp_name)),
    overwrite = TRUE)
  
  # ---- Visualization Layer. ----
  cat("   [Visualization]\n")
  try({
    p_forest <- sjPlot::plot_model(FINAL_MODEL, type = "est",
                                   show.values = TRUE, show.p = TRUE,
                                   title = sprintf("%s [%s] coefficients",
                                                   erp_name, exp_version)) + theme_bw()
    ggsave(file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("Forest_%s_%s.pdf", exp_version, erp_name)),
           p_forest, width = 7, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)
  })
  
  try({
    pd <- as.data.frame(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ offer_type * emotion, at = at_list))
    p_emm <- ggplot(pd, aes(x = emotion, y = emmean,
                            color = offer_type, group = offer_type)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, position = position_dodge(0.2)) +
      geom_point(size = 3.5, shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 2,
                 position = position_dodge(0.2)) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = emmean - SE, ymax = emmean + SE),
                    width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.2)) +
      scale_color_manual(values = colors_off, labels = labels_off) +
      scale_x_discrete(labels = labels_emo) +
      labs(title = sprintf("%s %s: emotion x offer_type", exp_version, erp_name),
           y = "Amplitude (\u00B5V)", x = "Emotion condition")
    ggsave(file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("Plot_%s_%s.pdf", exp_version, erp_name)),
           p_emm, width = 8, height = 6, device = cairo_pdf)
  })
  
  cat("   >>> Component complete.\n")
  invisible(FINAL_MODEL)
}

# ==============================================================================
# Multi-component side-by-side table for manuscript supplementary.
# Mirrors the convention of presenting all ERP components in a single tab_model
# HTML which can be opened in Word for final formatting.
# ==============================================================================
report_stage1_multi <- function(model_list, exp_version, out_dir) {
  if (length(model_list) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
  
  out_html <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("Stage1_AllComponents_%s.html", exp_version))
  out_md   <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("Stage1_AllComponents_%s.md", exp_version))
  
  # ---- HTML output via sjPlot::tab_model (preferred for manuscript supplementary) ----
  tab_model_succeeded <- FALSE
  tryCatch({
    sjPlot::tab_model(
      model_list,
      show.se = TRUE, show.stat = TRUE, show.ci = FALSE,
      string.se = "SE", string.stat = "t-value", string.p = "p-value",
      show.re.var = TRUE, show.obs = TRUE, show.icc = FALSE,
      show.r2 = TRUE, show.loglik = TRUE, show.dev = TRUE,
      emph.p = TRUE, p.style = "numeric_stars",
      file = out_html,
      dv.labels = names(model_list)
    )
    # Verify file actually exists. tab_model can silently fail on some sjPlot
    # versions or with mixed-class model lists, returning NULL without writing.
    if (file.exists(out_html) && file.size(out_html) > 0) {
      cat(sprintf("[Multi-component HTML] %s\n", basename(out_html)))
      tab_model_succeeded <- TRUE
    } else {
      cat(sprintf("[WARN] tab_model returned without error but no file written: %s\n",
                  out_html))
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[WARN] tab_model failed: %s\n", conditionMessage(e)))
  })
  
  # ---- Markdown fallback: assemble a side-by-side ANOVA table ----
  # Always produced, regardless of tab_model success. Provides a
  # version-independent manuscript-ready table that can be pasted into Word.
  tryCatch({
    rows <- list()
    methods_log <- character(0)
    for (comp_name in names(model_list)) {
      mdl <- model_list[[comp_name]]
      
      # Defensive class upgrade. Mirrors the upgrade in fit_stage1_bates;
      # protects against models loaded directly from RDS without going
      # through the engine.
      if (inherits(mdl, "merMod") && !inherits(mdl, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
        mdl_upgraded <- tryCatch(
          lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(mdl),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
        if (!is.null(mdl_upgraded)) mdl <- mdl_upgraded
      }
      
      # Per-component cascade: Satt -> KR -> Wald.
      anova_obj <- NULL
      method_used <- NA_character_
      
      # Attempt 1: Satterthwaite.
      anova_obj <- tryCatch({
        res <- suppressWarnings(anova(mdl, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
        if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
          method_used <- "Satterthwaite F"
          res
        } else {
          NULL
        }
      }, error = function(e) NULL)
      
      # Attempt 2: Kenward-Roger.
      if (is.null(anova_obj)) {
        anova_obj <- tryCatch({
          res <- suppressWarnings(anova(mdl, type = 3, ddf = "Kenward-Roger"))
          if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
            method_used <- "Kenward-Roger F"
            res
          } else {
            NULL
          }
        }, error = function(e) NULL)
      }
      
      # Attempt 3: Wald.
      if (is.null(anova_obj)) {
        anova_obj <- tryCatch(
          car::Anova(mdl, type = 3, test.statistic = "Chisq"),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
        if (!is.null(anova_obj)) method_used <- "Wald chi-square (LMM fallback)"
      }
      
      if (is.null(anova_obj)) next
      
      methods_log <- c(methods_log, sprintf("%s: %s", comp_name, method_used))
      
      apa <- format_anova_apa(anova_obj, mdl)
      apa$Component <- comp_name
      apa$Status    <- component_status(comp_name)
      apa$Method    <- method_used
      rows[[comp_name]] <- apa[, c("Component", "Status", "Effect",
                                   "APA_Report", "eta2_partial_95CI",
                                   "Sig", "Method")]
    }
    
    if (length(rows) > 0) {
      combined <- do.call(rbind, rows)
      writeLines(
        c(sprintf("# Stage 1 ANOVA Summary, %s", exp_version),
          sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
          "",
          "Type III ANOVA tests. LMM analyses use a Satterthwaite -> ",
          "Kenward-Roger -> Wald cascade (lmerTest, pbkrtest, car). All EEG",
          "analyses are LMM (Gaussian on amplitude); GLMM is not used.",
          "Component Status indicates confirmatory (present in both E1 and",
          "E2) vs exploratory (E2-only or E1 offer-locked).",
          "",
          "## Methods used per component:",
          paste0("- ", methods_log),
          "",
          knitr::kable(combined, format = "markdown",
                       caption = sprintf("Stage 1 fixed-effect tests across %d ERP components.",
                                         length(rows)))),
        con = out_md
      )
      cat(sprintf("[Multi-component Markdown] %s\n", basename(out_md)))
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[WARN] Markdown multi-component summary failed: %s\n",
                conditionMessage(e)))
  })
  
  invisible(list(html_ok = tab_model_succeeded, html_path = out_html, md_path = out_md))
}
```

``` {r stage2-blup}
# ==============================================================================
# 6. Stage 2: BLUP-based Individual-Difference Correlations
# ==============================================================================
#
# Subject-level random slopes from the Stage 1 model are extracted as best
# linear unbiased predictors (BLUPs). Each BLUP represents one subject's
# deviation from the population-level effect for that condition contrast.
# BLUPs are then regressed against trait variables in a between-subject
# framework. This two-stage approach is preferred over single-stage 3-way
# moderation given the limited number of subjects relative to the number of
# trait variables tested (typical ERP individual-differences practice).
#
# Multiple testing across the (component x BLUP-term x trait) cross-product is
# controlled via Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Spearman rank correlation is reported
# alongside the parametric weighted regression as a distribution-robust check.
# ==============================================================================

extract_blups <- function(model, erp_name) {
  ranef_obj <- lme4::ranef(model, condVar = TRUE)
  
  if (!"participant_id" %in% names(ranef_obj)) {
    cat(sprintf("[Stage 2] No participant-level random effects in %s; skipping.\n",
                erp_name))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  re_pid <- ranef_obj$participant_id
  if (ncol(re_pid) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Conditional variance structure depends on the random-effects specification:
  #   * Single (... | id) term  -> postVar is a 3-d array [n_terms, n_terms, n_subj]
  #   * Multiple separate terms -> postVar is a list of such arrays, one per term,
  #                                 with column-grouping recoverable from the term
  #                                 indexing in the 'nms' attribute.
  # We handle both cases below. In all cases we extract the per-subject standard
  # deviation (sqrt of diagonal) for each BLUP column, used as weights in Stage 2.
  pv <- attr(re_pid, "postVar")
  n_terms <- ncol(re_pid)
  n_subj  <- nrow(re_pid)
  cond_sd_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_subj, ncol = n_terms)
  
  if (is.null(pv)) {
    # No condVar attribute available; leave SDs as NA (Stage 2 falls back to
    # unweighted regression).
  } else if (is.list(pv)) {
    # Multi-term ZCP-style structure: pv is list of arrays, one per random term.
    # Column ordering in re_pid matches: term1's columns, then term2's, etc.
    col_offset <- 0
    for (term_idx in seq_along(pv)) {
      arr <- pv[[term_idx]]
      term_dim <- dim(arr)[1]  # number of columns from this term
      for (i in seq_len(n_subj)) {
        block <- as.matrix(arr[, , i])
        diag_vals <- if (length(block) == 1) as.numeric(block) else diag(block)
        cond_sd_mat[i, (col_offset + 1):(col_offset + term_dim)] <- sqrt(diag_vals)
      }
      col_offset <- col_offset + term_dim
    }
  } else {
    # Single-term structure: pv is a 3-d array.
    for (i in seq_len(n_subj)) {
      block <- as.matrix(pv[, , i])
      diag_vals <- if (length(block) == 1) as.numeric(block) else diag(block)
      cond_sd_mat[i, ] <- sqrt(diag_vals)
    }
  }
  
  colnames(cond_sd_mat) <- colnames(re_pid)
  
  blup_long <- re_pid %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("participant_id") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -participant_id,
                        names_to = "term", values_to = "blup_value")
  
  sd_long <- as.data.frame(cond_sd_mat) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(participant_id = rownames(re_pid)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -participant_id,
                        names_to = "term", values_to = "blup_se")
  
  dplyr::left_join(blup_long, sd_long,
                   by = c("participant_id", "term")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(component = erp_name)
}

# ==============================================================================
# Stage 2 between-subject correlation engine.
#
# Implements grouped FDR correction: traits are partitioned into theoretically
# meaningful groups (configured at top of script via stage2_trait_groups), and
# Benjamini-Hochberg FDR is applied independently within each group. This
# separates confirmatory tests on theory-driven traits from broader exploratory
# tests, preventing the dilution of statistical power that would result from
# correcting all traits jointly.
#
# Inputs:
#   blups_df:      long-format from extract_blups, one row per (subject, term, comp)
#   df_traits:     one row per subject; columns include traits listed in
#                  stage2_trait_groups
#   out_dir:       parent directory; per-group subdirectories are created here
#   trait_groups:  named list mapping group_name -> character vector of trait
#                  column names (defaults to the global stage2_trait_groups)
#   sig_threshold: cutoff for the 'significant' subset table (default 0.10
#                  matches interaction_threshold)
#
# Outputs (per group):
#   <group_name>/stage2_full_results.md           all (comp x term x trait) tests
#   <group_name>/stage2_significant_results.md    cells passing sig_threshold
# Output (combined):
#   STAGE2_REPRODUCIBILITY.txt                    methodology and group counts
# Returns:
#   Named list of results data frames (one per group), invisibly.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: core (component x term x trait) correlation loop. Produces an
# unadjusted long-format results table; FDR is applied by the caller within
# each group. Min-N threshold (10) prevents unstable estimates on sparse cells.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
compute_blup_trait_table <- function(blups_target, df_traits, traits) {
  results <- list()
  
  available <- intersect(traits, names(df_traits))
  if (length(available) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  merged <- blups_target %>%
    dplyr::left_join(df_traits, by = "participant_id")
  
  for (comp in unique(merged$component)) {
    for (term_name in unique(merged$term[merged$component == comp])) {
      sub_data <- merged %>%
        dplyr::filter(component == comp, term == term_name)
      
      for (trait in available) {
        if (!trait %in% names(sub_data)) next
        
        # Build a single working frame with the trait column renamed to a fixed
        # name. This avoids passing .data[[trait]] into lm(), which does not
        # support the rlang pronoun outside dplyr contexts.
        work <- sub_data %>%
          dplyr::select(participant_id, blup_value, blup_se, trait_value = !!trait) %>%
          dplyr::filter(!is.na(trait_value), !is.na(blup_value))
        
        if (nrow(work) < 10) next
        
        # Weighted regression: weights = 1/SE^2 down-weight high-uncertainty BLUPs.
        # Standard practice for two-stage individual-difference models with
        # uncertainty propagation (Goldstein, 2011).
        wts <- if (all(!is.na(work$blup_se)) && all(work$blup_se > 0)) {
          1 / (work$blup_se^2)
        } else {
          rep(1, nrow(work))
        }
        
        m_lm <- tryCatch(
          lm(blup_value ~ scale(trait_value), data = work, weights = wts),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
        
        # Spearman: distribution-robust corroboration for the parametric test.
        sp <- tryCatch(
          suppressWarnings(
            cor.test(work$blup_value, work$trait_value, method = "spearman")
          ),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
        
        if (is.null(m_lm) || is.null(sp)) next
        
        coefs <- summary(m_lm)$coefficients
        if (nrow(coefs) < 2) next
        
        results[[length(results) + 1]] <- data.frame(
          component  = comp,
          blup_term  = term_name,
          trait      = trait,
          n          = nrow(work),
          beta       = coefs[2, "Estimate"],
          beta_se    = coefs[2, "Std. Error"],
          t_stat     = coefs[2, "t value"],
          p_param    = coefs[2, "Pr(>|t|)"],
          rho_spear  = unname(sp$estimate),
          p_spear    = sp$p.value,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      }
    }
  }
  
  if (length(results) == 0) return(NULL)
  do.call(rbind, results)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main entry point: grouped Stage 2 driver.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_stage2_blup_correlation <- function(blups_df, df_traits, out_dir,
                                        trait_groups = NULL,
                                        sig_threshold = NULL) {
  if (is.null(blups_df) || is.null(df_traits)) {
    cat("[Stage 2] Insufficient input; skipping.\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  # Resolve defaults from global config.
  if (is.null(trait_groups)) {
    if (!exists("stage2_trait_groups")) {
      stop("[Stage 2] No trait_groups argument and stage2_trait_groups not defined.")
    }
    trait_groups <- stage2_trait_groups
  }
  if (is.null(sig_threshold)) {
    sig_threshold <- if (exists("interaction_threshold")) interaction_threshold else 0.10
  }
  
  # Exclude (Intercept) BLUPs: reflect overall amplitude, not condition-specific
  # deviations of theoretical interest.
  blups_target <- blups_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!grepl("^\\(Intercept\\)$", term))
  
  if (nrow(blups_target) == 0) {
    cat("[Stage 2] No condition-specific BLUPs available; skipping.\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  cat(sprintf("\n[Stage 2] Grouped analysis across %d trait group(s):\n",
              length(trait_groups)))
  for (gname in names(trait_groups)) {
    available_in_group <- intersect(trait_groups[[gname]], names(df_traits))
    cat(sprintf("  %-25s traits available: %d/%d\n",
                gname, length(available_in_group), length(trait_groups[[gname]])))
  }
  
  # ---- Per-group analysis loop ----
  group_results <- list()
  group_summary <- list()
  
  for (gname in names(trait_groups)) {
    group_dir <- file.path(out_dir, gname)
    if (!dir.exists(group_dir)) dir.create(group_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    
    group_traits <- trait_groups[[gname]]
    
    cat(sprintf("\n  >>> Group: %s\n", gname))
    
    raw_table <- compute_blup_trait_table(blups_target, df_traits, group_traits)
    
    if (is.null(raw_table)) {
      cat(sprintf("      No valid (comp x term x trait) cells in this group; skipping.\n"))
      group_summary[[gname]] <- data.frame(
        group = gname, n_tests = 0, n_sig_05 = 0, n_marginal_10 = 0,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
      next
    }
    
    # FDR within this group only.
    raw_table$p_param_fdr <- p.adjust(raw_table$p_param, method = "BH")
    raw_table$p_spear_fdr <- p.adjust(raw_table$p_spear, method = "BH")
    raw_table$Sig_param   <- add_sig_stars(raw_table$p_param_fdr)
    raw_table$Sig_spear   <- add_sig_stars(raw_table$p_spear_fdr)
    raw_table$group       <- gname
    raw_table             <- raw_table[order(raw_table$p_param_fdr), ]
    
    n_sig_05 <- sum(raw_table$p_param_fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
    n_sig_10 <- sum(raw_table$p_param_fdr < sig_threshold, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    cat(sprintf("      %d tests; %d FDR p < 0.05; %d FDR p < %g.\n",
                nrow(raw_table), n_sig_05, n_sig_10, sig_threshold))
    
    group_summary[[gname]] <- data.frame(
      group = gname,
      n_tests = nrow(raw_table),
      n_sig_05 = n_sig_05,
      n_marginal_10 = n_sig_10,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
    # Write per-group output tables.
    full_disp <- kill_scipen(beautify_labels(raw_table))
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(full_disp, format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Stage 2 [%s]: full BLUP x trait table (within-group FDR).",
                                     gname)),
      con = file.path(group_dir, "stage2_full_results.md")
    )
    
    sig_subset <- raw_table[raw_table$p_param_fdr < sig_threshold, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(sig_subset) > 0) {
      sig_disp <- kill_scipen(beautify_labels(sig_subset))
      writeLines(
        knitr::kable(sig_disp, format = "markdown",
                     caption = sprintf("Stage 2 [%s]: cells passing FDR p < %g.",
                                       gname, sig_threshold)),
        con = file.path(group_dir, "stage2_significant_results.md")
      )
    }
    
    group_results[[gname]] <- raw_table
  }
  
  # ---- Combined reproducibility log ----
  sink(file.path(out_dir, "STAGE2_REPRODUCIBILITY.txt"))
  cat("# Stage 2 Reproducibility Metadata (Grouped FDR)\n")
  cat("# Generated:", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n\n")
  cat("## Multiple-testing strategy:\n")
  cat("FDR method:           Benjamini-Hochberg, applied INDEPENDENTLY within each group.\n")
  cat("Significance cutoff:  ", sig_threshold, "(values < 0.05 marked confirmatory)\n")
  cat("Min N per cell:        10 subjects\n")
  cat("Weights:               1 / blup_se^2\n")
  cat("Robust check:          Spearman rank correlation\n\n")
  cat("## Trait groups:\n")
  for (gname in names(trait_groups)) {
    available_in_group <- intersect(trait_groups[[gname]], names(df_traits))
    cat(sprintf("  %-25s [%d traits available / %d configured]: %s\n",
                gname,
                length(available_in_group),
                length(trait_groups[[gname]]),
                paste(available_in_group, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  cat("\n## Per-group test counts:\n")
  if (length(group_summary) > 0) {
    summary_df <- do.call(rbind, group_summary)
    print(summary_df, row.names = FALSE)
  }
  cat("\n## BLUP terms tested:\n")
  cat("  ", paste(unique(blups_target$term), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("\n## Components included:\n")
  cat("  ", paste(unique(blups_target$component), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  sink()
  
  cat(sprintf("\n[Stage 2] Completed across %d groups. Output: %s\n",
              length(group_results), out_dir))
  
  invisible(group_results)
}
```
